subject: SLO questionnaire: measurement methodology, latency definitions, and crediting
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-12-11T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: SLO questionnaire: uptime, latency, credits

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this RFP over the finish line with us. Our security and procurement teams handed over a brief SLO/SLA questionnaire we need answered for our legal review. The PDF lists some specific asks but the items we most care about are below — can you confirm these and provide sample calculations/evidence for the last 6 months?

Key asks:
- Monthly uptime definition and measurement window (how do you compute "availability" across regions?)
- Latency commitments (p50/p95/p99) for sync generation requests; how are streaming responses measured?
- Credit calculation: formula, caps, and claim process (what evidence will you provide?)
- What telemetry and retention do you provide (raw traces, sampled spans, request logs)?

Can you return this as a short doc with examples? We need to include it in our commercial terms packet by Friday.

Attached: acme-slo-questions.pdf (our questionnaire)

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Senior IT Procurement, Acme Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-11T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLO questionnaire: uptime, latency, credits

Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise response we can include in the packet; I also attached two supplemental artifacts (slo-calculation-examples.csv and telemetry-schema.md) with worked examples from the last six months and our telemetry schemas. If you want a one-page version for legal, we can produce that too.

Summary answers (plain language):

1) Monthly uptime (availability)
- Commitment: 99.95% monthly availability for the Redwood API endpoint(s) serving a customer account in a single region.
- Measurement window: We compute monthly availability using calendar-month buckets (UTC).
- Measurement method: numerator = total healthy seconds (service responding with 2xx/3xx or 4xx) across the monitored endpoint; denominator = total seconds in the month, excluding scheduled maintenance windows (see maintenance section). We exclude customer-initiated network interruptions beyond our control per the attribution rules in the next section.
- Multi-region: For multi-region routing (active/active), availability is measured per-region and for cross-region SLA we provide an aggregated view with a per-request attribution policy (requests considered served if a healthy replica responded within route latency bounds).

2) Latency commitments
- Targets (typical for generation APIs; model/instance class specific in contract appendix):
  - p50: <= 120ms
  - p95: <= 350ms
  - p99: <= 900ms
- Definition: latency = time from request received by Redwood edge to final response byte emitted (for non-streaming requests). For streaming requests we expose both first-byte latency (time to first chunk) and completion latency (time to final chunk). Contract will specify which percentile(s) apply.
- Sampling & percentiles: We compute percentiles over request-level latencies during the 1-minute sampling granularity and then aggregate to the calendar-month percentiles using weighted request counts (see attached slo-calculation-examples.csv). We retain raw request-level metrics for 90 days and sampled traces for 180 days.

3) Credit calculation & claim process
- Trigger: A monthly availability shortfall below the committed threshold (99.95%) triggers credits.
- Formula: Credit % of monthly service fee = max(0, min(25, round(((SLA_target - Measured_availability) / SLA_target) * 100, 2))) — i.e., proportional to the shortfall, capped at 25% of the monthly fee. Example worked through in attachment.
- Exclusions: credits not applicable for force majeure, scheduled maintenance (we provide calendar + 48h notice for maintenance >15 minutes), customer misconfiguration, and third-party provider failures outside Redwood control (detailed attribution rules attached).
- Claim process: Customer opens a billing claim case via our portal within 30 days of month close and provides the claim period and impact summary. Redwood provides telemetry artifacts (sampled request logs, aggregated percentiles, internal incident timeline) within 10 business days. Credits applied within next invoice cycle if claim validated.

4) Telemetry and evidence
- Telemetry: per-request logs (sampled), latency histograms (per-route, per-model), ingest/egress timestamps, error codes, and span-level traces for sampled requests.
- Retention: raw per-request logs: 90 days; sampled 1:10 traces with full spans: 180 days; aggregated histograms and dashboards: 24 months (configurable for enterprise).
- Evidence we provide: time-series of availability/latency, raw request samples bounded to claimed incident window, trace samples showing client->edge->backend timeline, and a summary incident report from our SRE team.

Additional notes:
- Measurement independence: our SLA calculations are derived from our observability pipeline before customer-side networking (we do not include client-to-edge network noise in availability unless evidence shows service unable to respond). For disputed attributions we can run joint packet-level or synthetic tests.
- Canary/rollout deviations: transient errors during controlled rollouts are excluded if they meet our rollout policy thresholds (we will share rollout timelines).

Attachments: slo-calculation-examples.csv; telemetry-schema.md

If that looks good I can convert into a one-page section for the commercial terms. Otherwise let me know what you want expanded.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability & Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-12T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLO questionnaire: uptime, latency, credits

Rishi —

Thanks, this is exactly the level of detail our legal team wants. A couple of quick clarifications before we finalize:

1) Streaming responses: for use cases where we stream tokens back (and the request is long-running), do you compute p95/p99 on first-byte or on completion? If both, which one is used for credits?

2) Caching/prefix-KV: if your platform serves responses from KV/prefix cache (significantly faster), are cached requests included in the latency percentiles used for the SLO? Our concern is masking backend regressions with a large cache hit rate.

3) Evidence format: can you give an example ticket of what Redwood will hand over — e.g., a CSV with timestamps and latency_ms, or do you provide a signed doc?

If you can answer those three points we can mark the questionnaire complete.

Best,
Sara

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-13T14:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLO questionnaire: uptime, latency, credits — clarifications

Hi Sara —

Following up on Rishi's note, a few concrete clarifications for your legal and engineering reviewers:

Streaming measurement
- We publish both metrics: first-byte latency (time to first token/chunk) and completion latency (time to final token). For streaming-enabled routes the SLO will specify which metric governs credits; default for contract language is completion p95/p99 unless a customer explicitly requests first-byte for their use-case.
- Reasoning: completion latency better represents total user-perceived time for long-running generations; first-byte is useful for UX-sensitive workloads (progressive display).

Caching & percentiles
- Cache handling: cached responses are included in the percentile calculations because they are part of the customer experience. To avoid masking backend regressions we provide a breakdown (cached vs origin) in the monthly report. For contractual observability we provide both (1) overall percentiles and (2) origin-only percentiles (requests that missed cache). Customers can elect to have credits computed on origin-only in the contract appendix.

Evidence deliverable
- Artifact set (standard):
  - CSV: request_id,timestamp_ms,route,model,latency_ms,status_code (sampled window for the claim period)
  - Aggregated histograms and percentiles (JSON/CSV) for the full month
  - Trace bundle (for sampled traces) in OpenTelemetry format where applicable
  - SRE incident summary (PDF) that maps telemetry to our internal outage timeline
- All artifacts are digitally signed by the Redwood SRE lead for the claim window and delivered through our secure portal.

I'll attach a short ruleset for streaming measurement and a sample CSV we hand over. If you'd like, we can redact production IDs and provide a sanitized example for legal review immediately.

Attachment: streaming-latency-rules.pdf

Thanks — I'll coordinate a sanitized evidence sample and send it to procurement.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Manager, Observability & SLOs
Redwood Inference
